observations: The source text of LM2 Torah 56 is two sentences long and contains no explicit bechina (parallel-aspect) equating language. The teaching presents a single theological argument: a person with a Jewish heart (לֵב יִשְׂרְאֵלִי) transcends spatial limitation, because Divinity (הָאֱלֹקוּת) resides in the heart, and God — who is called 'the Place of the World' (מְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם) — is not contained by the world but contains it. Therefore one with a Jewish heart shares in this transcendence. To qualify for a new package, the spec requires at least 3 concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain. The four concepts present in the text — לֵב יִשְׂרְאֵלִי, הָאֱלֹקוּת, מָקוֹם, and מְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם — are not connected to each other through bechina (shared-nature) equating formulas. Their connections are: (a) Divinity is located inside the heart (indwelling relation, not bechina); (b) the one with a Jewish heart mirrors God's transcendence of place (logical inference, not bechina); (c) God is identified as 'מְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם' (a rabbinic title, not a bechina equating statement between two distinct mapped concepts). None of these relationships satisfy the symmetric shared-nature test that defines bechina. No new packages are warranted.
